en.headline: Man arrested after woman treated for suspected botulinum poisoning
en.dek: A 41-year-old man was held in Tsim Sha Tsui on suspicion of practising medicine illegally and possessing Part I poisons after a 35-year-old woman fell ill following a facial injection.
body: Police arrested a 41-year-old local man in Tsim Sha Tsui on Wednesday afternoon on suspicion of illegal medical practice and possessing Part I poisons, after a woman was hospitalised with suspected botulinum toxin poisoning.

The Centre for Health Protection said on Monday it was investigating a suspected case involving a 35-year-old woman who received what was described as a botulinum toxin injection to her face on 17 September inside a residential unit in Far East Mansion on Middle Road. She attended Queen Elizabeth Hospital the next day with drooping eyelids, breathing difficulty and weakness in her limbs, and remained in stable condition under treatment.

Tsim Sha Tsui officers and Department of Health staff carried out a joint operation at about 1.30pm on Wednesday. Five boxes of medicines classified as Part I poisons were seized. The man, surnamed Tam, was granted bail and must report back in late October. The case remains with the district miscellaneous enquiries team.

Police said practising medicine without registration, if it causes personal injury, can carry up to seven years’ imprisonment under the Medical Registration Ordinance. Unlawful possession of a Part I poison can bring a fine of HK$100,000 and two years’ jail. Officers advised the public not to seek injections or other treatment from unlicensed practitioners.

zh.headline: 尖沙嘴女子注射肉毒後不適 41歲男涉非法行醫被捕
zh.dek: 警方聯同衞生署在尖沙嘴拘捕一名譚姓男子，涉嫌非法行醫及管有第一部毒藥，檢獲五盒藥劑，已准保釋候查。
body: 警方周三下午在尖沙嘴拘捕一名41歲本地男子，涉嫌非法行醫及管有第一部毒藥。事件源於一名35歲女子接受報稱肉毒桿菌毒素注射後不適入院。
衞生防護中心周一公布正調查該宗懸疑肉毒中毒個案。女子於9月17日在中間道遠東大廈一個住宅單位面部接受注射，翌日出現眼瞼下垂、呼吸困難及四肢無力，到伊利沙伯醫院急症室求診，目前留院情況穩定。
尖沙嘴警區雜項調查小隊聯同衞生署人員周三下午約1時30分採取行動，在現場檢獲五盒屬第一部毒藥的藥劑。譚姓男子已獲准保釋，須於10月下旬向警方報到。
警方表示，根據《醫生註冊條例》，非註冊人士進行醫學治療並導致他人受傷，最高可判監禁七年；根據《藥劑業及毒藥條例》，非法管有第一部毒藥可處罰款10萬元及監禁兩年。警方呼籲市民勿向無牌人士求診或接受注射。
